threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep referring to the Overground as the ‘train’ and not knowing that you should hang out at the local pubs to catch the real vibe.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded us with opera. The bus was packed but we all ended up clapping as we rolled past Effra Road.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner mixed with a hint of exhaust on Sonnenallee at midnight. That's when I realized this place has a pulse like no other.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a nightclub in a former public toilet next to a busy street. It’s a wild blend of nightlife and urban history.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they curse at the BART delays like it's an old friend let them down again, not a stranger's fault.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading passengers on the 31 Balboa with an old guitar—strumming 'Hotel California' while we crept through rush hour. Pure SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can enjoy Gràcia’s plazas at any hour, but locals know they turn into echo chambers of loud, late-night chatter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment when the tram rattles through a quiet street and the locals barely flinch.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the tube' instead of 'the overground' and only know the Clapton end of the canal. Give it a few months.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in a tutu serenading a streetlamp on the 35 last night. Just another night in Brixton, really.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted a 70-year-old man expertly juggling oranges at the tempelhof park, while his dog watched, totally unimpressed.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a döner kebab shop with a dance floor, packed with locals busting moves at 3 AM. It's a real Kreuzberg experience.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to navigate BART delays like it's a game—dodging the crowds while newcomers panic at the schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy singing opera on the 38 Geary. Everyone stopped scrolling on their phones and just listened. Moments like that remind you we’re all in this together.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Sagrada Família, but it’s the little squares, like Plaza del Sol, where the real community buzzes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they pause at crosswalks, waiting for the light to change, as locals just bolt across without a second thought.
